title: Mix-and-match cross-encoder fallback policy and scale validation for global rerank endpoint
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Background: The reranking endpoint is increasingly serving heterogeneous traffic across locales and request shapes. We have multiple cross-encoder variants (compact, medium, full-precision) and documented latency/quality trade-offs, but the current routing rules are coarse: either the heavy model or the compact fallback. This ticket designs and validates a mix-and-match fallback policy that chooses per-request candidate models based on locale, prefix-length, and KV-cache hit rates, and validates it under scale to avoid regressions.

Objectives:
- Define a deterministic fallback policy that combines: locale preference, token budget, KV cache hit probability, and cost tier. The policy must be safe and explainable.
- Implement a lightweight decision layer in the rerank router to pick cross-encoder variants per request and to fall back gradually by fraction.
- Build an automated scale and regression harness that exercises multilingual traffic patterns, measures p50/p95 latency, throughput (req/s), and quality delta (MRR/NDCG) vs baseline.
- Produce rollout plan with canary windows, automatic rollback if quality drops >1.5% MRR or latency SLO violations exceed 5% of requests.

Success criteria / Acceptance:
- No more than 1% absolute drop in baseline MRR on our closed eval set per locale after rollout (preferred <0.5%).
- Latency p95 for rerank endpoint remains within current SLO (+10% headroom) during expected traffic and scaled tests.
- Successful automated ramp to 100% on staging and canary phases with no manual intervention required.
- Playbook for rollback and mitigation documented in Console runbook.

Approach:
1) Policy design: implement a small decision tree that takes signals (locale tag, total candidates, KV-cache-hit boolean, estimated token-length) and returns prioritized model variants and an ordered fallback list.
2) Router integration: add policy code to the routing layer (stateless decision, no added DB lookups) and allow feature flags per customer/route.
3) Regression harness: reuse the rerank eval harness with synthetic multilingual traces (based on production sampling) and scale to 5x peak qps on staging clusters. Track both quality and token+inference cost.
4) Validation & KPIs: run A/B tests with shadow traffic; compare MRR/NDCG by locale and latency percentiles; instrument per-decision telemetry to validate policy choices.

Trade-offs considered:
- Running medium models by default improves quality but increases cost and KV cache churn. We mitigate by preferring compact models for short candidate lists and for locales with historically smaller gains.
- More complex ML-based routing could yield better per-request choices but increases ops surface and hard-to-debug regressions; we will start with a rule-based policy and later explore learned routing as a follow-up.

Rollout plan:
- Staging: 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-06 run full scale tests (5x peak) using synthetic traces.
- Canary: start 2025-03-10 with 1% traffic, increase to 10% after 24h if no regressions, 50% after 48h, 100% after 72h.
- Automatic rollback triggers: total MRR drop >1.5% on any top-5 locale OR latency p95 > SLA for >5% of requests during a 30m window.

Monitoring and alerting:
- Add telemetry: policy_decision, chosen_model_variant, kv_cache_hit, per-request latency, and quality tags on a sampled subset.
- Dashboards: rerank/mrr-by-locale, rerank-latency-p50-p95, model-variant-distribution.

comments: 2025-02-18 - Kickoff: Aligning on policy signals with PM and Research. Decided to start rule-based approach to reduce ops risk (Leah).
2025-02-21 - Research ran locale-specific ablations showing compact model loses 0.9points MRR on ja/ko but <0.2 on en/es. We will prioritize medium model for ja/ko when candidate list >8 (Monica).
2025-02-26 - Prototyped router decision function in branch feature/rerank-policy. Initial microbench shows ~2ms added wall time in router for policy decision; acceptable (Arjun).

2025-02-28 - Q/A on staging: KV cache eviction increase observed when medium model fraction >30%. Added mitigation to prefer compact variant when estimated KV cache miss probability >0.6 (SRE flagged risk).
2025-03-01 - Drafted canary thresholds and rollback triggers with Product (Eve). Added automatic rollback in router orchestrator to flip feature flag if alerts fire.
2025-03-02 - Started scheduling staged scale runs for 2025-03-03; perf harness will generate 3M rerank requests with locale distribution sampled from production (Arjun).
notes: Plan avoids any per-customer DB lookups in decision path to keep router horizontally scalable.
If policy proves insufficient in 4 weeks, follow-up ticket will scope a lightweight learned router (research + offline training).
Customer Escalation: One enterprise customer (acme-corp) has expressed sensitivity to small MRR drops in ja/ko locales—coordinate canary schedules with them.
